# Loading

Loading useful packages

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
```

The centred log-ratio is defined by hand so that the transformation is
transparent and has no hidden zero handling. It is identical to
`compositions::clr()` for strictly positive compositions.

```{r}
clr <- function(x) {
  stopifnot(all(x > 0))
  lx <- log(x)
  lx - mean(lx)
}
```

Loading raw data

```{r}
raw_data <- read.csv("validations-reseau-ferre-profils-horaires-par-jour-type-2eme-trimestre.csv", sep = ";")
colnames(raw_data)
```

# Recovering altered data

```{r}
raw_data <- raw_data %>% mutate(
  ID_ZDC = if_else((
    CODE_STIF_ARRET == "ND" & 
      CAT_JOUR == "SAVS" & 
      CODE_STIF_TRNS == "100"
  ),
  71799, 
  ID_ZDC
  ),
  LIBELLE_ARRET = if_else((
    CODE_STIF_ARRET == "ND" & 
      CAT_JOUR == "SAVS" & 
      CODE_STIF_TRNS == "100"
  ),
  "PTE D.BAGNOLET", 
  LIBELLE_ARRET
  ),
  CODE_STIF_RES = if_else((
    CODE_STIF_ARRET == "ND" & 
      CAT_JOUR == "SAVS" & 
      CODE_STIF_TRNS == "100"
  ),
  "110", 
  CODE_STIF_RES
  ),
  
  CODE_STIF_ARRET = if_else((
    CODE_STIF_ARRET == "ND" & 
      CAT_JOUR == "SAVS" & 
      CODE_STIF_TRNS == "100"
  ),
  "684", 
  CODE_STIF_ARRET
  )
)
```

# Column selection and translation

Selecting appropriate columns and translating them

```{r}
data <- raw_data %>% mutate(
  station_id = paste(
    CODE_STIF_TRNS, 
    CODE_STIF_RES, 
    CODE_STIF_ARRET, 
    sep = "_")
) %>% select(
  station_id,
  ID_ZDC,
  LIBELLE_ARRET,
  CAT_JOUR,
  TRNC_HORR_60,
  Pourcentage_validations
) %>% rename(
  connection_id = ID_ZDC,
  station_name = LIBELLE_ARRET,
  day_cat = CAT_JOUR,
  time_slot = TRNC_HORR_60,
  percentage_entering = Pourcentage_validations
)

head(data)

unique(data %>% pull(time_slot))
```

Transforming time slots into start time points

```{r}
ts_to_stp <- c(
  "0H-1H"= 0,
  "1H-2H"= 1,
  "2H-3H"= 2,
  "3H-4H"= 3,
  "4H-5H"= 4,
  "5H-6H"= 5,
  "6H-7H"= 6,
  "7H-8H"= 7,
  "8H-9H"= 8,
  "9H-10H"= 9,
  "10H-11H"= 10,
  "11H-12H"= 11,
  "12H-13H"= 12,
  "13H-14H"= 13,
  "14H-15H"= 14,
  "15H-16H"= 15,
  "16H-17H"= 16,
  "17H-18H"= 17,
  "18H-19H"= 18,
  "19H-20H"= 19,
  "20H-21H"= 20,
  "21H-22H"= 21,
  "22H-23H"= 22,
  "23H-0H"= 23
)

data <- data %>% mutate(
  time_slot = ts_to_stp[time_slot]
)
```

Translate day categories:

- WD: Working day (outside of school holidays periods)

- WDSH: Working day during school holidays

- SA: Saturday (outside of school holidays periods)

- SASH: Saturday during school holidays

- SUPH: Sunday and bank holidays

```{r}
translate_day_cat <- c(
  "JOHV" = "WD",
  "JOVS" = "WDSH",
  "SAHV" = "SA",
  "SAVS" = "SASH",
  "DIJFP" = "SUPH"
)

data <- data %>% mutate(
  day_cat = translate_day_cat[day_cat]
)
```

# Removing wrong data

## Removing non-defined data

Removing unknown stations

```{r}
data <- data %>% filter(station_name != "Inconnu")
```

Checking `connection_id`

```{r}
any(is.na(data$connection_id))
```

There are non-defined connections, let's inspect them

```{r}
data %>% filter(is.na(connection_id))
```

It is normal since there are no connection zone in the Orly Airport, we will handle it later.

Checking that there is only one `station_name` per `station_id`

```{r}
data %>% select(station_id, station_name) %>% group_by(station_id) %>% distinct(station_name) %>% count() %>% filter(n != 1)
```

Checking `day_cat`

```{r}
unique(data$day_cat)
```

Checking `time_slot`

```{r}
data %>% filter(is.na(time_slot))
```

The corresponding percentage is null, they do not carry information so we discard them

```{r}
data <- data %>% filter(!is.na(time_slot))
```

Inspecting `percentage_entering`

```{r}
data %>% filter(is.na(percentage_entering) | percentage_entering < 0 & percentage_entering > 100)
```

Checking that all day types exists for each station

```{r}
data %>% select(station_id, day_cat) %>% distinct() %>% group_by(station_id) %>% count() %>% ggplot(data = ., aes(n)) + geom_bar()
```

## Removing inconsistent data

Checking that all distributions sum up to 100%

```{r}
data %>% group_by(station_id, day_cat) %>% summarise(tot = sum(percentage_entering)) %>% ggplot(data = ., aes(tot)) + geom_bar()
```

There is some inconsistency (probably associated to number rounding), we will correct it later. Checking if all points exists

```{r}
data %>% group_by(station_id, day_cat) %>% count() %>% ggplot(data = ., aes(n)) + geom_bar()
```

Checking which time point is mostly missing

```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(time_slot)) + geom_bar()
```

Given that every distributions sums up to approximately 100%, we can add missing points by giving them a zero value.

```{r}
data <- data %>% complete(
  time_slot, 
  day_cat, 
  nesting(station_id, 
          connection_id, 
          station_name
  ), 
  fill = list(percentage_entering = 0.)
)
```

Checking zero values

```{r}
data %>% filter(percentage_entering == 0) %>% ggplot(data = ., aes(day_cat)) + geom_bar()
```

```{r}
data %>% group_by(time_slot) %>% summarize(zero_freq = mean(percentage_entering  == 0)) %>% plot()
```

There is no clear cut-off, we transform all zero values in near-zero values.
Shares are reported with two decimals, so a recorded 0 means a true share
below 0.005%. We replace it with 0.01 and keep an explicit `imputed` flag, so
that later steps know exactly which values are replacements (a genuine 0.01
and an imputed one are otherwise indistinguishable).

```{r}
imputation_value <- 0.01

data <- data %>% mutate(
  imputed = percentage_entering == 0,
  percentage_entering = ifelse(imputed, imputation_value, percentage_entering)
)

mean(data$imputed)
```

We check normalization

```{r}
data %>% group_by(station_id, day_cat) %>% summarise(tot = sum(percentage_entering)) %>% ggplot(data = ., aes(tot)) + geom_bar()
```

```{r}
data %>% group_by(station_id, day_cat) %>% summarise(error = (sum(percentage_entering)-100)/0.01)
```

The totals differ from 100 because of rounding and of the zero replacement.
We **close** each composition deterministically, $x \mapsto 100\,x/\sum_t x_t$.

An earlier version corrected the rounding error by subtracting random
multinomial draws of 0.01. That approach had two problems: it could push
imputed 0.01 values back to exactly 0 (which makes the CLR infinite), and,
without a seed, it changed the data on every knit. Closure avoids both. It
keeps every value strictly positive, it is reproducible, and it does not
change the CLR at all, because the CLR is scale invariant:
$\mathrm{clr}(c\,x)=\mathrm{clr}(x)$.

```{r}
data <- data %>%
  group_by(station_id, day_cat) %>%
  mutate(percentage_entering = 100 * percentage_entering / sum(percentage_entering)) %>%
  ungroup()

data %>%
  group_by(station_id, day_cat) %>%
  summarise(tot = sum(percentage_entering), .groups = "drop") %>%
  summarise(max_abs_error = max(abs(tot - 100)),
            min_share = min(data$percentage_entering))
```

# Creating useful data containers

3D array with rows as stations, columns as day types and cells (or depth) as the hourly distribution

```{r}
to_array_3d <- function(data, value_col) {
  data %>% select(
    station_id,
    day_cat,
    time_slot,
    all_of(value_col)
  ) %>% pivot_wider(
    names_from = day_cat,
    values_from = all_of(value_col)
  ) %>% {split(.[setdiff(names(.), "time_slot")], .$time_slot)} %>%
    map(~ .x %>%
          column_to_rownames('station_id') %>%
          as.matrix) %>%
    simplify2array
}

array_3d <- to_array_3d(data, "percentage_entering")
array_3d_imputed <- to_array_3d(data, "imputed")   # TRUE where a 0 was replaced

stopifnot(identical(dimnames(array_3d), dimnames(array_3d_imputed)))
```

3D array with Centred Log Ratio Transformation applied (full day, 24 hours)

```{r}
array_3d_clr <- aperm(apply(array_3d, c(1, 2), clr), c(2, 3, 1))
dimnames(array_3d_clr) <- dimnames(array_3d)
```

## CLR on service hours

At night most stations are closed, so most values between 1:00 and 4:59 are
replacements. In CLR coordinates such a value becomes
$\log(0.01)$ minus the log geometric mean, a large negative number fixed by
the replacement constant rather than by the data. A depth or bicluster
computed on the full day would then group stations mainly by *whether they
close at night*.

```{r}
imputed_by_hour <- apply(array_3d_imputed, c(2, 3), mean)
round(imputed_by_hour, 2)
```

We keep the hours in which, for **every** day type, at most 25% of the
values are replacements. Because the CLR is not subcompositionally coherent,
we re-close the subcomposition on those hours before taking the CLR. Simply
dropping columns of the full-day CLR would be wrong.

```{r}
hours_all <- as.integer(dimnames(array_3d)[[3]])
hours_service <- hours_all[apply(imputed_by_hour, 2, max) <= 0.25]
hours_service

array_3d_service <- array_3d[, , as.character(hours_service)]
array_3d_service <- sweep(array_3d_service, c(1, 2),
                          apply(array_3d_service, c(1, 2), sum), "/") * 100
array_3d_clr_service <- aperm(apply(array_3d_service, c(1, 2), clr), c(2, 3, 1))
dimnames(array_3d_clr_service) <- dimnames(array_3d_service)
```

## Integrity checks

```{r}
checks <- c(
  all_shares_positive        = all(array_3d > 0),
  full_day_sums_to_100       = max(abs(apply(array_3d, c(1, 2), sum) - 100)) < 1e-8,
  full_day_clr_finite        = all(is.finite(array_3d_clr)),
  full_day_clr_sums_to_0     = max(abs(apply(array_3d_clr, c(1, 2), sum))) < 1e-8,
  service_sums_to_100        = max(abs(apply(array_3d_service, c(1, 2), sum) - 100)) < 1e-8,
  service_clr_finite         = all(is.finite(array_3d_clr_service)),
  service_clr_sums_to_0      = max(abs(apply(array_3d_clr_service, c(1, 2), sum))) < 1e-8,
  # scale invariance: CLR of the un-closed service shares is the same
  service_clr_scale_invariant = isTRUE(all.equal(
    array_3d_clr_service,
    {
      raw <- array_3d[, , as.character(hours_service)]
      out <- aperm(apply(raw, c(1, 2), clr), c(2, 3, 1))
      dimnames(out) <- dimnames(raw)
      out
    }
  ))
)
checks
stopifnot(all(checks))
```

Tibble with station information

```{r}
stations <- data %>% select(
  station_id, 
  connection_id, 
  station_name
) %>% distinct()
```

# Saving cleaned data for next steps

```{r}
write.csv(data, "cleaned_data.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(stations, "stations.csv", row.names = FALSE)
save(array_3d, array_3d_imputed, file = "array_3d.rda")
save(array_3d_clr, file = "array_3d_clr.rda")
save(array_3d_clr_service, array_3d_service, hours_service,
     file = "array_3d_clr_service.rda")
```

To load data contained in `.rda` files, use for example `load("array_3d.rda")`. It will load `array_3d` (and `array_3d_imputed`) in the environment.

| File | Objects | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `array_3d.rda` | `array_3d`, `array_3d_imputed` | closed shares (%), 24 hours, and the replacement mask |
| `array_3d_clr.rda` | `array_3d_clr` | CLR on the full day (sensitivity analyses only) |
| `array_3d_clr_service.rda` | `array_3d_clr_service`, `array_3d_service`, `hours_service` | **CLR on service hours: use this for depth and biclustering** |
